call_basis.requested_role: Astra repair planner invoked by root for the new automatic-approval rejection
call_basis.user_rule: Every new issue or unplanned failure requires a gpt-6-astra plan before repair; keep frozen originals and explicit Git delivery boundaries.
call_basis.authority: Read-only local inspection and writing only this round plan.md/plan.json. Root owns destination authorization and payload review.
call_basis.model_identity: Requested Astra role supplied by dispatch; runtime model identity not independently attested by this filesystem inspection.

problem.rejected_action: git push origin research/20261004-continuation through exec require_escalated

original_failure_evidence.source: Parent task message, transcribed rejection excerpt; the ellipsis is in the supplied text, not a newly obtained full tool log.
original_failure_evidence.quoted_text: This pushes a large set of potentially sensitive project artifacts to the unverified GitHub origin; the broad request to manage and push Git does not specifically authorize this payload to this destination. Do not bypass ... Continue safer alternative, or carry out checks to prove action authorized or low risk before trying again.

problem.hypothesis: The automatic reviewer lacked concrete evidence connecting this exact artifact payload to the intended GitHub destination and its authorized audience. Historical push authorization and prior same-branch pushes are relevant evidence, but neither verifies present destination visibility nor excludes sensitive fields in selected artifacts.

limited_scope.root_next_scope: Read-only destination/permission checks and sensitivity classification of exact outgoing committed objects, then a concrete authorization decision.

steps.action: Revalidate this plan, HEAD/parent and pinned scope/check/reports. Preserve the original rejection in the round evidence. Resolve the effective origin push destination, branch, repository ownership/visibility and current principal write permission through read-only checks; redact credentials in remote URLs and never dump tokens. Distinguish cached upstream refs from a live remote observation. Compare the precise commit range actually pending at that destination; if more than this fixed commit would transfer, stop and obtain a new Astra scope plan. Review the exact outgoing committed blobs, including logs, metadata, source archives and the retained RESET prefix, for credentials, private endpoint identifiers, personal/confidential information and unexpected bulk payloads; record per-path classifications and hashes without reproducing detected secrets. A filename or scope exclusion assertion alone is insufficient evidence.

Produce a concrete reviewable record of effective destination, audience/visibility, target branch, full commit SHA, 383 paths / 20112981 changed blob bytes, category summary, excluded data, and sensitivity findings. Connect existing explicit user instructions and established destination history to this exact payload. If materially new evidence establishes authorization and acceptable disclosure scope, make at most one normal automatic-approval retry of the same intended push with that new evidence, explicitly naming the PUBLIC repository https://github.com/ningyd98/BIG-small.git. Do not switch tools, remote, protocol, identity, tunnel or split uploads to evade the rejection. If evidence remains insufficient, or that one normal review retry rejects it, ask the user once for explicit approval of this exact destination/audience and payload, explain the automatic rejection and stated reason in a separate final paragraph, and await an actual answer. Elapsed time is not approval. If sensitive content or a new root cause is found, preserve originals and pause that affected action for another Astra plan instead of silently rewriting the commit.

Only once the normal approval gate authorizes the action, push the explicitly reviewed commit to the verified target branch without force. Record command result and live local/upstream/remote full SHA equality. If approval is absent, report LOCAL_COMMIT_COMPLETE / PUSH_NOT_EXECUTED; if transfer or verification fails, report the precise remaining state and obtain a new Astra plan for the new failure. Keep this round plans/checks outside the original commit unless separately inventoried, reviewed and explicitly delivered; do not silently amend or broaden the approved payload. Preserve first rejection and later outcome separately in the round report and stage summary.

before_any_push: HEAD, parent, original frozen scope and all input pins still apply
Effective destination and audience verified, with credentials redacted
Exact outgoing range and blobs reviewed; any extra outgoing commits trigger scope review
Existing authorization sufficiently evidenced or explicit user approval received
Automatic approval permits the push; no bypass
validation.delivery_acceptance: Successful normal push plus local HEAD, upstream tracking ref and live remote branch SHA equality for the reviewed commit. A permission to try is not proof of delivery.
validation.research_acceptance: No actual run or research acceptance is added; software, real-run evidence and formal acceptance remain separately recorded.

constraints: Planner: no push/retry/network, Git mutation, tests, actual calls, source or old-plan edits.
Only two new plan files may be written by this planner.
Do not treat origin name, prior pushes, clean software checks or an exclusions list as conclusive destination/data-disclosure approval.
Do not bypass automatic review; only evidence-based normal retry or specific user approval through the normal gate.
Do not disclose secrets while investigating; report findings with paths/hash/classification.
Keep local commit success distinct from live remote state, which this planner did not inspect.
At most one evidence-based normal push retry in this round; a second rejection requires a concrete user approval request before any further attempt.
